title: The Warren Mammoth site (48LA3800): A non‐cultural terminal Pleistocene mammoth from southeastern Wyoming
content:
ABSTRACT

The Warren Mammoth site (48LA3800) in Laramie County, Wyoming, was excavated in 2022 and 2023 and preserves the remains of a single adult female Columbian Mammoth (Mammuthus columbi). Radiocarbon dates on bone collagen suggest an age of ca. 13 110 or 13 150 cal a BP, placing the animal's death just prior to the start of the Clovis period during the terminal Pleistocene. A small sample of possible lithic artifacts was identified during excavation, making the site a useful case study for the investigation of potential human association with the mammoth. To test the hypothesis of human presence at the site, we examined spatial association between lithic and bone distributions, morphological comparisons between surface and excavated lithics, and bone modifications. We find that the excavated materials are likely geofacts, resulting from downslope movement of cryptocrystalline silicates that naturally occur at the site. Rodent and carnivore tooth marks are present on some skeletal elements, but evidence for human bone modification is lacking. We conclude that the Warren Mammoth died of natural causes, not at the hands of human hunters, and that there is no firm evidence of human presence at the site.
